plan_review.notes: Reviewer found 2 blocking gaps: (1) router concurrency group lacked queue: max, so GitHub would drop pending events instead of queueing them under burst -- fixed by adding queue: max matching the ci-recovery.yml pattern; (2) TOCTOU race between dispatch and Actions-API visibility across serialized invocations, plus missing pending status -- fixed by adding pending to OUTSTANDING_RUN_STATUSES and a bounded waitForOutstandingCount poll before a dispatching invocation releases its concurrency slot. Both fixes verified by new unit tests.

rounds.notes: Blocking: queue:max unconditionally combined with a cancel-in-progress expression that can be true (flag-off schedule/workflow_dispatch path) -- GitHub rejects that combination, breaking the legacy/rollback path. Fixed by making queue conditional on MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED, matching where cancel-in-progress is guaranteed false. Non-blocking: (1) runFromEnv has no end-to-end test (accepted as pre-existing convention/out of scope), (2) dispatch-cap log used prNumbers.length instead of dispatchable.length (fixed), (3) waitForOutstandingCount comment overstated as airtight (reworded).

Verified blocking fix is genuinely correct (queue and cancel-in-progress expressions are mutually exclusive on MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED), confirmed non-blocking fixes, fresh full-diff pass found no new issues. 47/47 tests passing, lint clean.

Post-merge correction round: removed the trainEnabled->Infinity fallback from computeDispatchBudget per parent-session instruction (protection must not lapse when the merge-train feature is disabled). Reviewer confirmed: (1) no remaining path to Infinity from computeDispatchBudget; (2) unconditionally fetching scheduledPulls does not change collectPrNumbers' existing routing semantics; (3) trainQueueNonEmpty via queueEntries() is safe/fail-closed since that function is not gated by MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED; (4) making waitForOutstandingCount unconditional is a deliberate, documented tradeoff (extra API calls for closing the TOCTOU race in previously-unaffected paths); (5) the new 25-event train-disabled burst test and cap-of-2 unit tests correctly replace the old Infinity-asserting test, no stale assertions remain; (6) the new 'Known residual limitation' handoff section accurately describes the legacy/flag-off per-PR concurrency-group race, correctly scoped. One non-blocking observation: the train-disabled burst test is logically identical in code path to the train-idle-but-enabled burst test (both drive trainQueueNonEmpty:false) -- accepted as intentional documentation of the explicitly-requested scenario, not a distinct code path to prove. 48/48 tests passing, lint clean, verify:fast passed.
